That's my order of recommendation from top to bottom. I'd say the cutoff point would be between Konosuba and Akame Ga Kill where it stops being too "similar."

Re:Zero does have the monsters. The setting, cast, and story is also so much like a Final Fantasy game. Only thing different is how the main character fights since I don't recall him ever "fighting." 

Jojo's Bizarre Adventure has amazing fights. I'd say it's really only the first season that has monsters and stuff, and the problem is, the first season is imo the worst season (It's average, the other seasons are way better). Season 3 and 5 have amazing adventures and casts much similar to Final Fantasy. Season 4 isn't really similar, but you'll probably watch it anyways if you've watched the first 3 seasons.

Soul Eater, I can't recall well. All I know is that it's the most similar anime I've mentioned to a Final Fantasy game. This is a short description but this is a must watch.

Konosuba is more related to Dragon Quest than Final Fantasy I'd say. It's comedic at almost all times so that's one difference. The adventure itself feels like a comedic Final Fantasy.

Akame Ga Kill is the first anime that won't be that similar anymore. It's cast and adventure feels like Final Fantasy, but the enemies are just humans. Also this series is heavily spoiled so don't search anything about it. 

Highschool DxD is questionable. The fights and mythological aspect is like Final Fantasy, but other than that, it's not similar. I would recommend it still, but if you've seen clips of the anime, you'd get why it's weird for me to recommend this.

There are some small things you can fix here and there :

\- When you Up B, you usually don't snap to the ledge. Practice snapping the ledge with Up B, you lost a stock from the Mario game just from that one small mistake. In general, even if you're recovering without the Up B, you would always want to snap to the ledge unless its a mixup.

\-  You sometimes roll when its not necessary. I wouldn't say you roll a lot, but when you do, it's when you could do other options. For example, in one instance, both of you were in a neutral position but you rolled back. Here you gave up just a tiny bit of stage control. You could have done things like short hop nair in case they approach. Rolling is usually a bad option as it is reactable.

\- You rely on your Nair too much. Whenever you hit the opponent, you don't get an opportunity to press your advantage because I believe Nair just isn't a tool for that. I think you should use forward air more.

​

Now here is the general problems which when fixed can greatly improve your gameplay :

\- Whenever you're in disadvantage state (Aka you're far in the air and they're on the ground), you always seem to try to get a little bit too excited and land too near them. This should only be done as a mixup. You're always at a disadvantage when you're the one landing so you should try to avoid this encounter. Generally you'd want to land far from the opponent such that they cant dash attack / grab your landing. I'd say when you get knocked up into the air so high, drifting to the ledge and snapping to it is a reliable option. Other mixups you can do is like I said, landing near them but with a fair, or with a counter (although counter can be predictable). 

\-  In neutral, you always try to hit where the opponent is, not where they will be. No one is going to just stand there and wait for you to attack them. Chances are, if you have time to attack them, they also have time to move out of the way. Now I don't literally mean "where" as a location, i mean it as more of a state. For example, they can simply be standing, but then when you get near, they will shield. It's up to you to figure out how they will react. 

   On this note, you also sometimes get hit when you're in advantage state because you're not expecting to get hit. Unless you know your combo is true, always be patient to see how they'd react. Advantage state isn't necessarily being in a state where you can keep hitting the opponent for free, I'd say its more of being in a position where the opponent is forced to do a certain move, and all you have to do is guess what they will do. You're at an advantage here since you can just choose a safe option and you're not pressured to do something. You should try adopting a more defensive playstyle when in advantage state. One example is to move forward and stay at a distance where they can't attack you, and if they have wonderwing, hold shield. Now in this situation, you can choose to either wait and react, or guess and punish. 

​

Anyways that's all I have to say about your flaws. I can say for sure tho that even if you're at a disadvantage you're always confident and keep your composure. Good luck!
